findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same class — the added 4-param `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 silently redefines and replaces the 5-param `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145, so the 5-param form never exists at runtime because Ruby has no method overloading. Every existing caller that passes width and height separately — the old-signature call sites this diff preserves the 5-param def for, i.e. the thumbnail/optimized-image generation path (OptimizedImage.create_for and avatar flows) — now binds the integer height into `opts`, and `optimize`'s first expression `!!opts[:allow_animation]` raises TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer (Integer#[] with a Symbol), or ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4) when an opts hash is also passed; optimized-image creation crashes for every image upload, leaving posts without thumbnails and uploads erroring.

[BUG] `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` passed to `OptimizedImage.downsize` here is inert, because `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects the `_animated` instruction set when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, and `from` at this call site is `tempfile.path` — a Rack multipart tempfile (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart20150101-...) or a `discourse-upload-*` download tempfile — which never ends in `.GIF`. Any animated GIF between max_image_size_kb and 10MB is downsized by the static `downsize_instructions`, which resizes optimized delta frames without -coalesce/-deconstruct and produces garbled or corrupted animation; the allow_animated_thumbnails setting is silently ignored on the upload path.

[BUG] Hardcoding `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the per-type gate `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (which served both image and attachment uploads), while the server still enforces `max_attachment_size_kb` because the controller only downsizes images (`FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`). On any site with non-default limits, attachments between max_attachment_size_kb and 10MB now pass the client gate and then fail server-side with an alert claiming the max is 10MB, while attachments between 10MB and a raised max_attachment_size_kb (or a raised image limit) are blocked in the browser even though the server accepts them — admins' configured limits stop working.

[BUG] Hardcoding the API URL download cap to `10.megabytes` regresses API uploads on sites that raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB: `FileHelper.download` stops at its cap and raises, `rescue nil` sets tempfile to nil, and the following `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` evaluates `tempfile.size` on nil. An API client uploading a 10MB+ image by URL on a site with max_image_size_kb above 10MB gets NoMethodError: undefined method `size' for nil:NilClass, returning an HTTP 500, where this request previously downloaded and uploaded the file successfully up to the configured setting.

[BUG] The 413 handler now always reports the limit as a hardcoded 10MB, but with the client gate at line 182 also fixed at 10MB, any request that actually receives a 413 carried a file under 10MB (the proxy's body limit is below 10MB). Users whose upload is rejected by a proxy body limit under 10MB get a message saying the maximum is 10MB — a number their smaller file was already under — so the alert is wrong in every case it fires and tracks neither the site setting nor the real limit.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs up to five sequential ImageMagick subprocess invocations synchronously on the HTTP request thread — each one a full decode plus re-encode of a multi-megapixel image — instead of computing the required scale once. Every oversized (up to 10MB) image upload pins a unicorn worker for seconds while five converts run, so an attacker posting repeated 10MB images ties up all workers on a path that previously did zero in-request image processing (thumbnails were backgrounded); legitimate uploads also suffer up to five compounding lossy JPEG re-encodes (0.8^5 ≈ 33% linear) when a single computed geometry — or `-define jpeg:extent=<max>` — would hit the target size in one pass and delete the attempt counter and loop entirely.

[ADVISORY] This diff rewrites OptimizedImage's resize/downsize/optimize dispatch (merging the `dimensions` helper, changing `optimize`'s signature, adding a new downsize overload) and adds request-path image mutation in the uploads controller, but ships no test changes anywhere for either. A regression in this command-building API breaks optimized-image/thumbnail generation for every upload with no failing spec to signal it — the shadowed duplicate `downsize` in this very diff is exactly the class of error an existing `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` spec would have caught, and the next maintainer touching these signatures has no safety net.

[BUG] The class body now defines self.downsize twice — the preserved 5-argument def at lines 145-147 and the newly added 4-argument def at lines 149-152 — and Ruby silently keeps only the last definition, so the surviving method has signature (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) with arity 3..4 while the 5-argument wrapper is unreachable dead code. Every existing caller that passes max_width and max_height as separate arguments — the exact signature this same diff preserves at line 145, i.e. the thumbnail-generation call sites OptimizedImage.create_for was written against — raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4) at runtime, so post thumbnails and avatar optimized images stop being generated site-wide while the dead 5-argument wrapper misleads the next editor into editing a method that never executes.

[BUG] The pre-upload size check replaces the per-type gate Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with the hardcoded constant 10240, silently dropping the sibling settings max_avatar_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb that this same line used to enforce for non-image types. On default-configured sites, attachments and avatars above their real limits but under 10MB now pass the client check, transfer in full, and are rejected by the server — the new server-side downsize loop only covers images (FileHelper.is_image? gate) — so users pay a full 10MB upload for a file that used to be blocked instantly; conversely, admins who raised max_image_size_kb above 10MB have valid large images refused in the browser with an alert claiming the limit is 10MB, making their configured setting silently unenforceable.

[BUG] The downsize loop keys its target size on SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb while the type parameter is in scope, so avatar-typed uploads — which are images and therefore pass FileHelper.is_image? — get shrunk toward the image limit and are then size-validated by Upload.create_for against max_avatar_size_kb. An avatar larger than max_avatar_size_kb but under the new 10MB client gate sails through the client, burns up to five ImageMagick invocations shrinking toward the wrong limit, and is still rejected — the automatic-downsize feature silently no-ops for avatars while adding server work on every attempt.

[BUG] The while loop discards OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, and convert_with returns false whenever ImageMagick exits non-zero (return false if $?.exitstatus != 0), so a failed conversion is never detected anywhere in the loop. When convert cannot process the file (corrupt image, missing ImageMagick, unsupported pixel format), the loop retries four more times on the same poisoned tempfile and then falls through to Upload.create_for anyway; because the downsize writes in place (from == to == tempfile.path), a failed encode that partially wrote its output leaves a corrupt file that gets stored and served to users whenever its truncated size lands under the limit.

[BUG] The call passes allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails, but optimize selects the _animated instruction set only when from matches /\.GIF$/i and tempfile.path (a RackMultipart or Tempfile path with no extension) never matches that regex, so the flag is dead on this path and every animated GIF goes through the non-animated downsize instructions. Every oversized animated GIF upload is re-encoded through the non-coalesced instruction set — the separate _animated variant exists precisely because plain resizing corrupts delta-encoded GIFs — so the stored, served image comes out with misaligned frames or destroyed animation regardless of the site's allow_animated_thumbnails setting.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces a behavior-bearing mutation loop (five bounded attempts rewriting the upload in place), re-aritys OptimizedImage.downsize and optimize, and hardcodes the client limit, yet adds no verification: the only files touched are utilities.js, uploads_controller.rb and optimized_image.rb, with no spec/**, test/**, *.spec.* or *_test.* changes anywhere in the diff. The signature refactor ships unguarded — a single spec invoking the preserved 5-argument downsize would have raised ArgumentError on the duplicate definition before merge, and the loop's failure path, avatar-type path, and animated-GIF path now have no regression net, so the next refactor of downsize re-breaks uploads with no failing build.

[BUG] The 413 handler hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024, so the file_too_large alert reports a 10MB limit no matter which setting actually rejected the upload. A user whose 8MB attachment is rejected against a 4MB max_attachment_size_kb is told the limit is 10MB and retries an equally oversized file, failing again; likewise a user whose 6MB image passed the new 10MB client gate but could not be downsized server-side receives a message claiming the limit is 10MB — a number larger than the file they just uploaded.

[ADVISORY] The change converts a previously instant client-side rejection into a full transfer plus up to five sequential ImageMagick invocations executed synchronously inside the web request thread. Every composer image between max_image_size_kb and 10MB now holds a web worker for multiple seconds of convert CPU — a cheap amplification vector for an attacker posting 10MB images in bulk — and users who previously got an immediate alert now watch a multi-second hang per upload.

[ADVISORY] The new guard tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 acknowledges that a failed API URL download leaves tempfile nil, but three statements later Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...) dereferences that same nil. An API upload whose URL download fails still crashes with NoMethodError on nil.size and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx — the diff added nil-awareness to half the path (the downsize loop) and left the identical crash one statement below it.

[ADVISORY] The loop shrinks dimensions by 80% per iteration rather than shrinking file size, and after five attempts it gives up with no guarantee that re-encoding ever reaches SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Re-encodes that inflate file size (a low-quality-source JPEG re-encoded at ImageMagick's default quality, 16-bit PNGs) never converge, so a client-accepted sub-10MB image is still rejected as file_too_large after the server burns five convert runs — the user is left with no path to success despite the client's 10MB promise, and nothing in the diff verifies the implied acceptance criterion that every client-accepted image uploads.

[BUG] The API URL-download size cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, decoupling it from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb for every upload type. Sites whose admins raised max_image_size_kb above 10MB lose URL-based image uploads between 10MB and their configured limit — FileHelper.download aborts at the fixed cap, rescue nil yields a nil tempfile, and the request dies on the unguarded tempfile.size below — while attachment-type URLs are now fetched up to 10MB before being rejected against a much smaller max_attachment_size_kb.

[BUG] This diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same class — the 4-arg definition added here silently replaces the 5-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147 that this same diff just updated to the new `optimize` signature, so the width/height calling convention is destroyed and the `"#{max_width}x#{max_height}"` normalization on line 146 is unreachable dead code. In Ruby the later definition always wins, so both signatures cannot coexist: any caller still passing separate width and height values (the form the first definition was explicitly retained and rewritten to serve, e.g. thumbnail generation) now dispatches to the second definition, binding the height Integer into `opts`, where `optimize`'s `!!opts[:allow_animation]` raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) — every such call path crashes at runtime.

[BUG] The client-side check replaces the type-aware limit `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with the fixed `10 * 1024`, so it also governs attachment uploads (`type === 'attachment'`) even though this PR's server-side auto-downsizing (uploads_controller.rb) only shrinks files where `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. Non-image attachments between a site's `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB lose their only client-side enforcement: on server-enforced sites the full file is uploaded and then rejected (with the 413 alert now claiming the max is 10MB), and where the client was the enforcement layer the admin's attachment size policy is silently raised to 10MB — scope drift from a stated intent that covers only images.

[BUG] The 413 handler hardcodes the reported maximum as `10 * 1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so the alert states a limit that is not the server's actual body-size limit on any site whose effective limit is below 10MB. A user whose 5MB image is 413-rejected on a 1MB-limit site is told the max is 10240kb; every retry under that stated max fails again with the same lying message, with no indication of the real limit — previously the alert reflected the configured setting.

[BUG] The downsizing loop is bounded at a fixed five 80% resamples with no convergence guarantee, so uploads the client now permits (up to 10MB) can still exceed `max_image_size_kb` when it exits: five 80% steps scale pixel count to 0.8^10 ≈ 10.7%, leaving a 10MB PNG or animated GIF at ≈1.07MB — still over a 1024KB limit. Users on low-limit sites — the exact case the feature targets — still receive the generic 'file too large' rejection after five sequential ImageMagick subprocess runs of wasted server CPU per upload, and nothing in the UX distinguishes 'we tried shrinking and failed' from 'never allowed'.

[ADVISORY] `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is inert on this path: `optimize` selects the `_animated` instruction set only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, and `from` is `tempfile.path` — a RackMultipart temp file or a `discourse-upload-#{type}` download temp, neither of which carries a `.GIF` extension, so the gate can never match. The `allow_animated_thumbnails` setting has no effect on upload downsizing: oversized animated GIFs always run through the static instruction path, and the option passed here is implementation work untraceable to any behavior — the next reader will assume the setting is honored here and mis-debug animation loss.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing gate keys on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and on the API/URL path `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, so an oversized image served from an extensionless URL (e.g. `https://cdn.example.com/i/abc123`) is classified as non-image and skipped by the loop. API consumers uploading by URL — a common shape for CDN image URLs — silently miss the feature and their upload fails with a too-large error despite the client-side 10MB allowance, while the same image uploaded directly would be downsized; the feature under-covers the URL entry point this same controller serves.

[ADVISORY] The loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s return value even though `convert_with` returns `false` on a nonzero ImageMagick exit (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`) with all stderr discarded via `&> /dev/null`, and it converts in place by passing `tempfile.path` as both `from` and `to`. A failing convert (missing binary, corrupt input, disk full) is retried four more times on the same doomed command — five subprocess spawns per upload — and the request then proceeds with the untouched file; on a partial in-place write the truncated image, now smaller than the limit, passes the `tempfile.size` check on the next iteration and is stored and served corrupted.

[ADVISORY] `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap with a magic constant, creating a third independently-maintained 10MB value in this PR (alongside utilities.js lines 182 and 246) across two languages with no single source of truth and no settings surface. Sites with `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 can no longer fetch image URLs their policy allows, and the next person tuning the upload ceiling must find and edit all three constants in sync — miss one and the client wall, the 413 message, and the server download cap drift apart with no config entry to reconcile them.

[ADVISORY] The hardcoded 10MB client ceiling walls off image uploads on sites that configured `max_image_size_kb` above 10240, since the server would accept those files (the downsize loop only triggers above the setting) but the client now blocks them with 'max 10240kb'. An admin who raises `max_image_size_kb` to 20480 gets uploads blocked at 10MB with no setting anywhere that controls the new wall — the still-editable site setting now contradicts actual behavior and the admin cannot discover why uploads fail.

[ADVISORY] The PR rewrites the `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` call contract and adds an attempt-bounded in-place downsize loop on the hot upload path, with no spec anywhere in the diff exercising either the changed signatures or the new loop behavior. Exactly the class of regression this diff actually contains — the duplicate `downsize` definition clobbering the width/height form with a TypeError — passes review and CI because nothing invokes the changed contract, so a broken thumbnail-generation caller ships silently to production.

[BUG] The diff leaves two consecutive definitions of self.downsize in the same file — the pre-existing 4-arg def at line 145 (whose body the diff edits) and a new 3-arg def at line 149 — so Ruby keeps the second and silently discards the first, making the line-146 edit unreachable dead code. Every caller still using the old signature crashes at runtime: a 5-arg call (from,to,w,h,opts) raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4), and a 4-arg call binds the height Integer into the opts parameter and raises TypeError (Integer#[] with a Symbol) at optimize's opts[:allow_animation] on line 155 — any in-tree or plugin code invoking the documented 4-arg API breaks with no compile-time or test warning.

[BUG] The downsize loop bounds work by a hardcoded attempt count (5) and a fixed 80% geometry step whose product caps byte reduction at 0.64^5 (~10.7% of the original), and on exhaustion it falls straight through to Upload.create_for on line 72 with no post-loop size check. A 10MB upload against a site configured with max_image_size_kb below ~1MB (e.g. 256KB, needing a 39x reduction) is submitted for storage anyway at ~10x the limit after five sequential full re-encodes on the request thread; the same fall-through happens whenever a pass fails to reduce bytes (ImageMagick re-encode guarantees no shrinkage and convert_with's false return is ignored), so the feature's advertised invariant — stored uploads never exceed max_image_size_kb — is silently violated.

[BUG] The client-side size gate replaces the per-type site setting Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a hardcoded 10MB literal, decoupling the only client-side enforcement from site configuration. Sites with max_image_size_kb above 10MB are silently clamped (the server accepts a 25MB original untouched, but the UI blocks at 10MB), and max_attachment_size_kb loses its only enforcement point — the server never checked attachment sizes, so a site configured for 512KB attachments now stores 10MB attachments through the normal UI.

[BUG] The downsizing gate keys on FileHelper.is_image?(filename), where filename is File.basename(URI.parse(url).path) for API URL uploads and the client-supplied original filename for form uploads, rather than on detected content. An image fetched from an extensionless URL (dynamic endpoints, CDN transform URLs) passes the newly raised 10MB download cap but is never classified as an image, so the pre-diff behavior (refused above max_image_size_kb) becomes post-diff storage of the unshrunk oversized file — the gate decision rests on a name, not the bytes.

[BUG] The new re-encode loop has no server-side input-size bound: the only cap on the form-upload path is the client-side JS constant, and the loop condition on line 66 checks the target without ever limiting how large the input feeding up to five ImageMagick passes can be. A direct POST to /uploads (API client, curl, stale front-end) carrying a 100MB 'image.jpg' makes one request drive five sequential convert invocations sized by that input on a Rails request thread — minutes of worker CPU per request from any ordinary logged-in user, exhausting workers under modest concurrency, where pre-diff this path did no per-file image processing at all.

[BUG] The allow_animation option passed to OptimizedImage.downsize is a no-op at this call site: optimize (line 155) selects the animated instruction path only when from matches /\.GIF$/i, but from is tempfile.path — a RackMultipart path for form uploads or 'discourse-upload-<type>' for URL downloads — which never ends in .GIF. downsize_instructions_animated is unreachable from this entire feature, so SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails never affects upload downsizing and every oversized animated GIF is re-encoded through the frame-naive non-animated path, skipping the coalesce/animation-aware pipeline the codebase itself defines for GIFs and degrading the stored original.

[BUG] The API URL download cap changes from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes, creating a third independent copy of the 10MB limit (besides utilities.js lines 182 and 246) with no shared source of truth. Sites that configured max_image_size_kb above 10MB regress — URL uploads the old code fetched at up to the configured size are now refused at 10MB — and any future edit to one of the three literals silently desynchronizes client enforcement, server download cap, and error messaging.

[BUG] The 413 handler replaces SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb with a hardcoded 10240KB in the user-facing message, but 413 is produced by the web server's client_max_body_size, a limit no Discourse code reads from this constant. On any deployment whose web-server body limit differs from 10MB — for browser users a 413 only fires when the limit is below 10MB, since the JS gate already blocked larger files — the user is shown a maximum of 10240KB that no component enforces at that point, so the displayed cap is guaranteed wrong exactly when users need it.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing gate tests filename-is-image while ignoring the upload's type parameter, so image-named files uploaded as attachments are recompressed against max_image_size_kb instead of attachment policy. A site with max_attachment_size_kb=20MB and max_image_size_kb=4MB silently lossy-recompresses a 9MB photo attached as an attachment down to 4MB — attachments exist to preserve originals, so users receive degraded files with no indication that attachment fidelity is governed by the image setting.

[ADVISORY] The feature silently repurposes max_image_size_kb from a hard upload limit into a recompression target, while the actual new hard limit (10MB) exists only as literals and is not configurable anywhere. Operators cannot tune or disable the 10MB cap without a code deploy, and the settings UI still presents max_image_size_kb as the upload limit — an admin raising it to 25MB sees no effect through the UI while an admin lowering it unknowingly converts 'reject oversized uploads' into 'silently lossy-recompress every larger upload' for their users, with no settings rename, migration, or documentation of the semantic shift.

[ADVISORY] All of the diff's new behavior-bearing logic — the convergence loop, the 80%-geometry refactor of OptimizedImage.optimize, and the downsize signature change — ships with no test anywhere in the diff. A regression in the instruction-string assembly or the loop bound ships silently to every site; the duplicate self.downsize definition and the unreachable allow_animation path that actually landed in this diff are precisely the failures a unit test over the downsize/optimize signatures would have caught before merge.

[BUG] Line 182 replaces the admin-configurable SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] upload gate with a hardcoded 10240KB for every upload type — including attachments, which this PR's server-side downsizing (gated on FileHelper.is_image?) never processes — silently deleting the accepted constraint that the client mirrors per-site configured limits, with no replacement setting or flag. Admins who configured limits above 10MB have valid uploads hard-blocked in the browser with no server-side 10MB rule to justify it; on default sites an 8MB attachment now passes the client check and transfers fully only to be rejected by the real 4096KB server limit, and attachments over 10MB are blocked by an alert claiming the maximum is 10240KB — an objective change (attachment gating, de-configurability) the PR title 'automatically downsize large images' never announced and that cannot be reverted without a code deploy.

[BUG] The 413 error handler now displays a hardcoded 10240KB as the maximum size instead of the site's actual SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the message no longer matches any server-enforced limit. A user on a default site whose 5MB attachment is rejected against the real 4096KB limit is told the maximum is 10240KB, retries the identical file, and fails again — where the old code reported the true configured limit on the first failure.

[BUG] The API URL-download size cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, replacing the admin-configurable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb bound, so remote-fetch payload limits are no longer configurable by site admins. An operator who deliberately set a small max_image_size_kb to bound inbound payload sizes now has API clients fetching up to 10MB per URL upload regardless of the setting, and this Ruby-side copy of the 10MB constant sits independently of the two JavaScript copies, so the three limits diverge the first time any one of them is changed.

[BUG] The diff defines self.downsize twice in the same class (lines 145-147 and 149-151); Ruby has no method overloading, so the second definition silently replaces the first, making the 4-arg 'converted' version unreachable dead code — and any caller still using the pre-PR signature downsize(from, to, width, height) binds the Integer height into opts and crashes in optimize at opts[:allow_animation] with TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer). The public contract of a core model method changed from numeric width/height to a geometry string with no working migration path: existing 4-arg callers get a confusing TypeError instead of a resize, and because the sibling resize(from, to, width, height) still takes numbers, the next caller naturally writes downsize(from, to, w, h) and hits the same crash while the dead def sits in the file implying both signatures are live.

[BUG] The new call passes allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails, but optimize routes to the animated instructions only when from =~ /\.GIF$/i, and from here is tempfile.path — an extensionless Rack/Tempfile path — so the option can never take effect on the upload-downsizing path this diff adds. Animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb are downsized through the static-image instructions instead of the animated path, and admins who enabled animated thumbnails see the setting silently ignored for uploaded GIFs; the option wired up in this diff is dead on arrival.

[ADVISORY] The new 10MB limit is hand-maintained in three independent copies across two languages — utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, and uploads_controller.rb:55 — with no shared constant, site setting, or feature flag binding them. Whoever next tunes the cap (say to 25MB) updates one copy and the client gate, the user-facing too-large message, and the server's URL-download cap silently disagree; operators cannot adjust or disable the downsizing scheme at all without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing loop discards OptimizedImage.downsize's false return value (convert_with reports ImageMagick failure via exit status), so a failed convert is indistinguishable from a successful one inside the loop. When convert fails on an image (corrupt input, missing binary), the controller relaunches the same failing command four more times and then hands the still-oversized file to Upload.create_for, so the user receives a misleading 'file too large' error while the actual failure — downsizing — goes unreported.

[ADVISORY] The server-side downsizing path has no input size bound of its own; the only 10MB cap is the client-side JavaScript check, so multipart API uploads feed arbitrarily large images directly into up to five ImageMagick convert passes. Before this diff an oversized image was rejected at validation with zero image processing; after it, an API caller uploading a huge image costs the operator up to five heavy convert invocations before rejection, bounded only by whatever proxy body limit the deployment happens to configure.

[BUG] The diff defines self.downsize twice in the same module — (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145 and (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 — and Ruby keeps only the last definition, silently discarding the 5-parameter one that existing width/height callers (thumbnail generation via OptimizedImage.create_for, whose call sites this diff does not touch) still invoke. Every existing caller passing separate width/height arguments now dispatches to the 4-param version: a 5-argument call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 4) and a 4-argument call binds the height Integer into opts and raises TypeError on opts[:allow_animation] — thumbnail generation for post images breaks site-wide while the controller's new 4-arg call works, so the breakage is invisible on the feature's own happy path.

[BUG] The server-side size enforcement is best-effort with no rejection path: the shrink gate keys on the client-supplied filename (FileHelper.is_image?(filename), where filename is the multipart original_filename or the URL basename), the false return of OptimizedImage.downsize on convert failure is ignored, the loop gives up after 5 attempts (five 80% resizes leave ~33% of the original pixels), and Upload.create_for is then called unconditionally with the tempfile regardless of whether the loop brought it under the limit. An oversized image whose client-controlled name doesn't look like an image, an image more than ~3x max_image_size_kb (a 10MB upload against a 512KB limit is still ~3.3MB after 5 passes), or any file whose convert fails is stored at full size, so SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb is not enforced and the admin's storage/bandwidth cap is silently exceeded.

[BUG] validateUploadedFiles now enforces a hardcoded 10 * 1024 KB instead of the per-type setting Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], and this diff adds no server-side size rejection to replace it for non-image types. An admin who configured max_attachment_size_kb (or any per-type limit) below 10MB to cap storage and bandwidth has that setting silently ignored in the standard UI — any user uploads attachments up to the web-server 10m cap — while admins who raised a setting above 10MB now see legitimate users blocked with an error claiming a 10MB maximum that is not the configured policy.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop performs up to 5 sequential full-resolution ImageMagick invocations synchronously inside the request thread on attacker-chosen input, with no pixel/byte sanity bound on the input and no early bail-out on repeated convert failures (one computed resize percentage collapses the 5 passes into one). Any user with upload permission submits a decompression-bomb image (a ~10MB PNG encoding a ~100-megapixel raster that ImageMagick expands into hundreds of MB of pixel buffer) or a file that resists compression, forcing 5 convert passes per request and exhausting web workers or OOM-killing the process under modest repeated uploads.

[ADVISORY] The size bound on the server-side fetch of the request-supplied URL is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, replacing the admin-configurable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The operator's only knob over how many bytes the server downloads from an untrusted, request-supplied URL is removed: with the site setting lowered to 1MB, the server still fetches up to 10MB per API request from any host, and the limit cannot be tuned or lowered without a code deploy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop performs up to 5 sequential full-resolution ImageMagick invocations synchronously inside the request thread on attacker-chosen input, with no pixel/byte sanity bound on the input and no early bail-out on repeated convert failures (one computed resize percentage collapses the 5 passes into one). Any user with upload permission submits a decompression-bomb image (a ~10MB PNG encoding a ~100-megapixel raster that ImageMagick expands into hundreds of MB of pixel buffer) or a file that resists compression, forcing 5 convert passes per request and exhausting web workers or OOM-killing the process under modest repeated uploads.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` adds a synchronous loop (`attempt = 5; while ...`) that can invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times on attacker-controlled uploads (`tempfile.path`), all within the request thread. The loop ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`convert_with` (which returns `false` on nonzero exit), so it will continue retrying even if ImageMagick repeatedly fails. The only guard is `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, which is a byte limit and does not bound image pixel complexity (allowing decompression-bomb style CPU/memory exhaustion within the 10MB cap shown elsewhere in the diff). This is a real, diff-grounded availability/security risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize guard triggers on any image-named file against max_image_size_kb, with no check of whether the upload is an attachment governed by max_attachment_size_kb. A user attaching an 8MB photo as a downloadable file on a site with max_image_size_kb=4096 but max_attachment_size_kb=51200 has their original silently replaced server-side by a lossy 80%-shrunk re-encode sized to the image limit — the full-resolution bytes are destroyed with no marker that a downsize occurred, and downloaders can never retrieve what was actually uploaded.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the newly added block downsizes any upload whose `filename` passes `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, regardless of the `type` argument or any attachment-size setting. It repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, overwriting the same tempfile path in-place before `Upload.create_for(...)`, which can permanently replace the originally uploaded bytes with a lossy re-encoded version. The diff shows no guard to limit this to image uploads vs attachments, and no indication/marker that a downsize occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loop discards OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so ImageMagick failures (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit status) are indistinguishable from an unsuccessful shrink. When convert fails — corrupt input, resource limits, security-policy refusal — the loop burns all five attempts (before any authorization or extension validation has run) and then hands the unchanged or partially-written tempfile to Upload.create_for, turning what should be a clear resize failure into a confusing downstream validation error or a corrupt upload attempt.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new retry loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` but ignores its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` returns the result of `convert_with(...)`, and `convert_with` explicitly returns `false` on non-zero ImageMagick exit status. Because the loop only checks `tempfile.size` and never checks for `false`, ImageMagick failures are indistinguishable from a no-op/unsuccessful shrink: it will burn all 5 attempts and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever is on disk (unchanged or potentially partially written), leading to confusing downstream errors/corrupt upload attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is dead at this call site because optimize() selects the animated instructions only when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, and tempfile paths (Rack multipart files and the 'discourse-upload-<type>' files created at line 55) never end in .gif. Oversized animated GIFs are resized through the single-frame instructions (no -coalesce/-layers Optimize), producing frame artifacts or broken animations for exactly the uploads the animated code path exists to handle.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb` the new downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, the animated code path is selected only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. For URL-based uploads, the tempfile is created via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, which (as shown) supplies a basename with no `.gif` extension, so `tempfile.path` will not match `\.GIF$` even if `filename` is a GIF. That makes `allow_animation` ineffective for that case and can route animated GIFs through the non-animated instructions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public model method downsize is silently redefined from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) to (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) with no rename or deprecation. Any existing caller passing numeric width/height (plugins or in-repo code outside this diff) now binds the height into opts, so opts[:allow_animation] in optimize raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) and the request 500s; a 5-argument old-style call raises ArgumentError outright.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `self.downsize` is defined twice. The later definition `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` overrides the earlier `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, silently changing the public API. Any existing callers still using the old 4-arg form will have `max_height` bound into `opts` (as an Integer), so `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` will raise (e.g., `TypeError`). Old 5-arg calls would now raise `ArgumentError` due to arity mismatch. This is directly verifiable from the diff and can cause 500s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 4-arg definition at line 145 — Ruby redefines methods and has no arity-based overloading — so the backward-compatible overload is dead code, and any caller still using the pre-diff `downsize(from, to, width, height[, opts])` form binds `height` into `opts` and crashes inside `optimize` at `opts[:allow_animation]` with NoMethodError (undefined method `[]` for Integer), or raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4) when an opts hash is also passed. Every remaining call site on the old signature — precisely the callers the retained first definition was written to serve — raises on each invocation instead of resizing, so image-resizing paths (e.g. thumbnail generation) fail at runtime while the diff looks backward-compatible.

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, the file defines `self.downsize` twice: first as `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later again as `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload by arity, so the second definition replaces the first, making the “backward-compatible” 4-arg form dead. Any existing caller using the old signature `downsize(from, to, width, height[, opts])` will now bind `height` into `opts`, and `optimize` will call `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will error if `opts` is an Integer; passing an additional opts hash would also raise an argument count error. This is a runtime-breaking change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop discards `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s failure return — `convert_with` returns false on any non-zero ImageMagick exit status (optimized_image.rb:162) and discards the command's output and stderr (`&> /dev/null`) — so a failed conversion is retried four more times unchanged and the still-oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for` with no check that the loop achieved anything. When ImageMagick fails (corrupt or mislabeled image file), the failure is invisible everywhere: nothing is logged, the user receives the generic 'file too large' rejection after five wasted convert spawns, and operators cannot distinguish 'image too big' from 'image processing broken'.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores its return value (`convert_with` returns `false` on non-zero exit). If ImageMagick fails, the tempfile is unchanged yet the loop keeps retrying up to 5 times and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without verifying the file was reduced or that conversion succeeded. The diff also shows `convert_with` suppresses all output via `&> /dev/null`, so failures are silent/undifferentiated as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The hardcoded `10 * 1024` replaces the per-type lookup `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for every `type` this validator runs with, not just images, so non-image uploads (attachments) are now client-side gated at 10MB regardless of the server-enforced per-type setting. On a site with max_attachment_size_kb below 10MB, an 8MB attachment passes client validation and only fails after a full upload round-trip when the server rejects it; on sites whose per-type limits exceed 10MB, valid uploads are blocked client-side with a false 'max 10MB' message.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js`, the client-side size check changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) while still being executed in a function parameterized by `type`. This means all upload types validated by this code path (not just images) are now capped/allowed at 10MB on the client, which can diverge from server/site settings (e.g., `max_attachment_size_kb`, other `max_<type>_size_kb`), causing false passes (server later rejects) or false blocks (client blocks valid uploads). The diff directly shows this behavior change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 alert now always reports the maximum as 10MB, but a 413 fires precisely because the request exceeded the actually enforced limit (the per-type setting — the pre-diff code reported `max_image_size_kb`), so the message misdescribes the real limit on every site where that limit differs from 10MB. A user whose 4MB attachment exceeds a 2MB server limit is told 'max 10MB', retries with a smaller-but-still-over-limit file, and hits the same failure — the error content actively misdirects the retry.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 handler changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB). That makes the alert always report 10MB regardless of the site’s configured max (`max_image_size_kb` / per-type limits), so on sites with a different configured limit the message will misstate the maximum. This is directly introduced by the diff (`case 413:` block).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loop gives up after five 80%-dimension passes regardless of whether the size target was reached — 0.8^5 is only a ~33% best-case floor and file-size reduction merely tracks the 64% per-pass area reduction, so it is worse for PNGs — so uploads larger than roughly 3x `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` are still over the limit when handed to `Upload.create_for`. On sites with max_image_size_kb below ~3.4MB, every large image upload burns five ImageMagick passes and then fails with the same 'file too large' error the feature was meant to eliminate — the promised automatic downsizing silently does not work for a whole class of site configurations.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing logic in `uploads_controller.rb` is explicitly capped (`attempt = 5` and `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`), so it can exit with `tempfile.size` still above the configured limit and then immediately calls `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)`. That means the “auto-reduce” behavior is best-effort and can still result in a too-large upload after spending up to five ImageMagick passes. However, the diff does not prove the specific numeric claims (~3x threshold, guaranteed failure for certain site settings), since actual file-size reduction per pass depends on image content/format and `OptimizedImage.downsize` implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is structurally inert on this path: `optimize` only selects the animated instruction set when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (optimized_image.rb:155), but `tempfile.path` never ends in `.gif` — Rack multipart tempfiles are named `RackMultipart...` and `FileHelper.download` names them `discourse-upload-<type>...` — so every animated GIF is processed with the non-animated instruction set here. The allow_animated_thumbnails setting has no effect when shrinking uploads: admins get silently different frame handling between the upload-shrink path and the thumbnail pipeline, and animated GIFs are resized with the instruction set the setting was meant to bypass.

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload-shrink loop (uploads_controller.rb), `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passes `from` as `tempfile.path`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated instruction set is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is truthy *and* `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The diff shows no renaming of the tempfile to preserve the original extension (it remains `file.tempfile` / `FileHelper.download(...)` output), so the decision is based on the tempfile filename rather than the original `filename`. This makes `allow_animated_thumbnails` ineffective (or at least unreliable) for GIF uploads on this path and can lead to animated GIFs being processed with non-animated instructions during shrink.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fixed 80%-per-pass loop re-encodes the image once per iteration — up to five sequential ImageMagick subprocess invocations and five lossy re-encodes inside the synchronous upload request — instead of computing the required scale once and resizing in a single pass; a file barely over the limit is needlessly cut to 80% linear dimensions. Users get visibly degraded uploads (generation loss from repeated JPEG re-encoding and needless resolution loss for near-limit files), and every oversized image adds up to five subprocess passes to request latency, pushing large-image uploads toward proxy timeouts.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` adds a synchronous loop (`attempt = 5; while ...`) that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` until the file drops under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Each call goes through `OptimizedImage.convert_with`, which shells out to ImageMagick (a subprocess) and rewrites the same file, so an oversized image can incur up to 5 sequential conversions within the upload request. Using a fixed "80%" per pass can also reduce resolution more than necessary for images only slightly over the limit, and repeated JPEG re-encodes can compound quality loss. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/quality concern rather than a functional correctness bug.
